Siddur builder

It has its own app now

Composing, setting and printing a siddur is a different job from learning in one — a different person, a different session, usually a different machine — and it was the heaviest thing in this app by a wide margin. Measured here on 20 August: opening this route mounted 21,254 extra nodes in 5,941 ms, paid for by everyone who came to read.

Open Meldar Siddur ↗ Open in this tab
What moved and what did not

The builder is the same engine, not a rewrite — it loads the same three modules this app does (the siddur data, the interlinear engine, the package layer) and copies none of them. Your saved siddur is the same document in the same place, so it opens there exactly as it stood here.

Nothing was deleted: this route still exists, the readers the paper importer borrows from the builder are untouched, and the benschers and the printed-page path stay here.

Sync is not a second code path: an envelope is built by the same pure builders as every export and delivered by the same interopAdapter target — syncPush · syncPull · syncStatus sit beside exportRoster · importRoster. Because a batch is grouped by orgId before it is built, one push carries exactly one institution; isolation is structural, not a promise. And no amount of queued teaching data adds up to a decision — that stays with the Beth Din.
